gloss: myriad; eight million; innumerable (especially of gods)

definitions.explanation: An extremely large, uncountable number. Most famously used in the Shinto concept of {八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ} (eight million gods / myriad deities), expressing the belief that divine spirits reside in all things.

examples.japanese: {八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ}。
{日本|にほん}には{八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ}がいると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that there are eight million gods in Japan.

examples.japanese: {八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ}という{考|かんが}え{方|かた}は、{自然|しぜん}のあらゆるものに{神|かみ}が{宿|やど}るという{信仰|しんこう}に{基|もと}づいている。
examples.english: The concept of myriad gods is based on the belief that divine spirits dwell in all things in nature.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ} (the myriad gods, the eight million deities)

USAGE NOTES:
Almost exclusively used in the expression {八百万|やおよろず}の{神|かみ}, a core concept in Shinto. The number "eight million" is not literal but represents an inconceivably large number — the idea that gods and spirits inhabit everything in the natural world: mountains, rivers, trees, rocks, and even everyday objects. This concept is foundational to Japanese animism and is often cited to explain Japan's polytheistic religious worldview. The reading やおよろず is an old Japanese number reading ({八百|やお} = 800, {万|よろず} = 10,000).
